To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) language-conditioned reinforcement learning is an efficient tool for the autonomous acquisition of skills; (ii) semantic representations are key to enable goal generation and language grounding in autonomous agents; and (iii) DECSTR is an efficient and robust language-conditioned reinforcement agent.

the proposed architecture allows an agent to autonomously ground language in a repertoire of skills by leveraging semantic representations of the environment and that this architecture is more efficient than an end-to-end approach and an approach using a non-semantic intermediate representation.

a language-goal-behavior architecture (L-G-B) is a promising framework for the autonomous acquisition of skill repertoires and that an intermediate semantic representation is a promising tool for the grounding of language to behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the acquisition of autonomous repertoires of behaviors.
the acquisition of a repertoire of skills and the grounding of language in these skills.
the development of a new architecture for language-conditioned reinforcement learning that allows to autonomously learn repertoires of behaviors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

LGB enables a new class of language-conditioned RL agents that are able to autonomously acquire a large repertory of skills and are able to satisfy language commands in multiple ways, even in the absence of any feedback from the environment or the user.
our approach is a step towards a new conceptual paradigm of LC-RL that allows autonomous learning, language grounding, and the generation of diverse behaviors.
the LGB framework is a promising approach for grounding language to autonomously acquired skills.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an approach to autonomous skill learning that is able to ground a symbolic language to an agent's actions via an intermediate semantic language.
the semantic intermediate representation helps the agent to learn more efficiently, to generalize better and to ground language better.
the proposed LGB architecture allows for a more efficient and autonomous acquisition of skills, and a more robust language grounding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intermediate representation of the world plays a crucial role in the autonomy and flexibility of language-conditioned RL agents.
semantic representations can be a powerful tool to ground language in a variety of ways, and that they can be autonomously acquired by intrinsically motivated agents.
the semantic representation of an environment is a key component to ground language to autonomously-acquired skills.
